title: Autogen Admin Sage Orchestrator: synthesize safe playlets from telemetry
creator: Avery Chen
description: Build an Autogen Orchestrator that converts observability signals and alert contexts into small, parameterized admin playlets (idempotent tasks) that frontline support can safely execute. The system will ingest traces/alerts, propose a templated playlet (shell/WASM step sequence + typed inputs + pre-checks), and surface it in the admin console and workbench. Focus areas: safe defaults, RBAC gating, dry-run simulation, telemetry-to-playlet mapping, and a lightweight review workflow for psychopy (ops) reviewers.
acceptance_criteria: Given an alert with structured context, the orchestrator proposes a playlet with at least one pre-check, one remediation step, and an assert step
Playlets are validated against a safety policy; unsafe constructs (e.g., unrestricted db-drop) are rejected with remediation tips
Support engineers can run a dry-run that executes all pre-checks and simulated remediation without mutating production
Audit log entries are emitted for proposal, approval, execution, and dry-run with request_id and tokenized inputs
Operator can approve-and-run a proposed playlet with RBAC enforcement and permission escalation tracking
Integration tests cover ingestion -> proposal -> dry-run -> approve-and-run paths in a sandbox cluster
technical_notes: Ingest signals from alerts API, trace correlation service, and console event stream; canonicalize into a PlayletContext schema
Playlet format: linearized step list (WASM step or packaged shelllet), typed inputs, pre-check predicates, expected invariants
Execution runtime: reuse micro-runflow runner (WASM sandbox) to ensure language-agnostic steps and process isolation
Safety sandbox: run pre-checks and a simulated remediation in a hermetic environment (mocked cloud/DB endpoints) before a real run
Policy engine: reuse existing guardrail rules (deny-list + transformation suggestions); extend rules to include token rate limits and sensitive-ops patterns
KV-cache cue: for frequently executed remediation (eg. prefix cache flush), suggest caching and backoff knobs to reduce blast radius
Telemetry hooks: emit structured events to tracing with tags: playlet_id, proposed_by=orchestrator, inputs_hash, review_state
Storage: proposals stored as immutable blobs with versioning and short-lived presigned links for reviewer artifacts
RBAC: tie approvals to SSO groups; track escalation via an approval chain (2-step for high-impact playlets)
Rollback: enable automatic compensating playlet generation for common remediations (if known) and surface rollback runbooks
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): Enable orchestrator for internal infra alerts only; proposals only (no run). Deploy 1 small team: infra-oncall
Phase 1: Add dry-run capability for a broader set of alerts (internal + non-customer-facing infra). Require a single approver for run requests
Phase 2: Allow approve-and-run for teams with elevated permissions; add 2-step approval for high-impact playlets
Phase 3: Expose in Console as "Proposed Playlets" sidebar with filters and review queue; enable opt-in for Dedicated customers
Observation windows: monitor for increased incident mean time to remediation (MTTR) and any unauthorized runs; roll back if safety metric breach
test_plan: Unit: PlayletContext canonicalizer tests for common alert shapes (prometheus, slog, trace)
Integration: end-to-end test in sandbox cluster: alert -> propose -> dry-run -> approval -> run with mocked producer/consumer
Fuzz: mutate inputs to ensure guardrail policy rejects malformed or unsafe playlets
Load: simulate 200 proposals/minute to verify dedupe and backpressure in the ingestion path
Security: red-team exercise to attempt privilege escalation via crafted playlet inputs
